# Kaṭṭhahārijātaka (Ja 7)

**ID:** Ja 7
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Kaṭṭhahārijātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The King and the Stick-Collector
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja7

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kaṭṭhahārijātaka* (Ja 7) is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to its commentary's framing narrative, the Buddha related this story while residing at Jetavana in connection with the story of Vāsabhakhattiyā (detailed further in the *Bhaddasālajātaka*, No. 465), which touches on King Pasenadi's reluctantly fulfilled request for a bride from the Śākyan clan [SuttaCentral; Levman 2014]. In the story of the past, King Brahmadatta of Benares encounters a lowly wood-gatherer or faggot-gatherer who conceives a son [Luce et al. 1970; Ohnuma 2012]. The virtuous mother performs an Act of Truth (*saccakiriya*) to compel the king to acknowledge his paternity, thereby securing the boy's rightful succession to the royal throne [Ohnuma 2012].

Scholars have noted that the core motif of this tale bears strong similarities to the well-known narrative of Śakuntalā in the *Mahābhārata*, as well as the Burmese romance of Thambhula and Kyanzittha [Luce et al. 1970]. The narrative also appears in Buddhist visual culture, including possible early depictions at Pagan and an illustrated mural of the royal procession from the temple of Kataluva in Sri Lanka [Luce et al. 1970; Buddhist Virtues 2011].

No internal Pali text-reuse matches are registered in the DharmaNexus database [DharmaNexus]. While SuttaCentral records no direct canonical parallels in other languages, automated cross-language text alignment by DharmaNexus identifies minor segmental reuses with the Sanskrit *Saṃghāṭa Sūtra* (reaching a maximum similarity score of 20), though these represent machine alignments rather than curated narrative parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].

- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus computed parallels for ja7 — Supplied absence of Pali-internal text reuse and machine alignments with the Saṃghāṭa Sūtra.

- [Luce et al. 1970] Gordon H. Luce, Bo-Hmu Ba Shin, and U Tin Oo, Old Burma. Early Pagan. Vol. 2 (1970) — Described the story of Brahmadatta and the wood-gatherer, early Pagan art, and parallels in the Mahābhārata and Burmese tradition.
